module_title: Feed Formulation for Specific Fish Species

lessons.title: Formulation for Tilapia
lessons.body: Tilapia is the most farmed fish in Africa, and it responds well to a simple, plantâbased diet. A typical starter feed for tilapia fry (0.5â5 g) should contain 35â40% crude protein. You can achieve this with local ingredients: 30% fishmeal (e.g., from Lake Victoria sardines), 25% soybean meal, 20% maize, 15% rice bran, 5% cassava flour, and 5% vitaminâmineral premix. For growâout (from 50 g to market size), reduce protein to 28â32%. A practical growâout mix: 15% fishmeal, 25% soybean meal, 30% maize, 20% rice bran, 5% palm oil, and 5% premix. Use a simple feed mill: a hammer mill to grind ingredients, a horizontal mixer, and a pelletizer. If you donât have a pelletizer, make moist dough balls by hand. In Africa, many farmers use a 2 mm pellet for fry and 4 mm for adults. Feed 3â5% of body weight per day, split into two meals. Tilapia can also utilize agricultural byâproducts like brewery waste, but limit to 10% to avoid poor water quality. Always test your feed: a good pellet holds together in water for at least 30 minutes. For a 100 kg batch, weigh: 30 kg fishmeal, 25 kg soybean meal, 20 kg maize, 15 kg rice bran, 5 kg cassava flour, 5 kg premix. Mix dry ingredients first, then add 15â20 litres of water to make a stiff dough. Extrude through a mincer or pellet mill. Dry pellets in the sun on a clean tarpaulin for 2â3 days until moisture is below 10%. Store in airtight bags in a cool, dry place. This formula works across Africa, from Nigeria to Uganda. Adjust fishmeal quality: if using local sunâdried fish, increase to 35% because protein content is lower. Never use spoiled fishmeal â it causes offâflavours and disease.

lessons.title: Formulation for Catfish
lessons.body: Catfish (Clarias and Heterobranchus) are carnivorous and need high protein. For fry (0â5 g), aim for 45â50% crude protein. A proven African formula: 40% fishmeal, 20% soybean meal, 15% groundnut cake, 10% maize, 10% blood meal, 5% vitaminâmineral premix. For growâout (from 20 g to 1 kg), reduce to 35â40% protein. A common growâout mix: 25% fishmeal, 20% soybean meal, 15% groundnut cake, 20% maize, 10% wheat offal, 5% fish oil, 5% premix. Catfish feed must be extruded (floating pellets) because they feed at the surface. If you donât have an extruder, make sinking dough balls â but expect slower growth and more waste. Use a feed mill with a 2 mm die for fry and 6 mm for adults. In Nigeria, many farmers use a local recipe: 30% fishmeal, 20% soybean meal, 20% groundnut cake, 15% maize, 10% cassava peel, 5% premix. Mix dry, add water (about 30% of dry weight), and pellet. Dry to <10% moisture. Feed 5â8% body weight daily for fry, 2â3% for adults. Catfish are aggressive; feed them at dusk and dawn. Always keep feed fresh â rancid oils cause liver damage. For a 50 kg batch of growâout feed: 12.5 kg fishmeal, 10 kg soybean meal, 7.5 kg groundnut cake, 10 kg maize, 5 kg wheat offal, 2.5 kg fish oil, 2.5 kg premix. This yields about 35% protein. Test protein with a simple kit or send a sample to a lab. In Africa, blood meal is a cheap protein source but must be dried and ground finely. Avoid using more than 10% blood meal â it can cause vitamin deficiency. Also, catfish need aeration; feed quality alone wonât work in poor water.

lessons.title: Formulation for Salmon and Trout
lessons.body: Salmon and trout are coldâwater carnivores, not native to most of Africa, but they are farmed in highland areas like Kenya, South Africa, and Lesotho. They need 40â45% protein and high energy. A typical trout feed: 35% fishmeal, 20% soybean meal, 15% wheat gluten, 10% fish oil, 10% maize, 5% vitaminâmineral premix, 5% blood meal. For salmon, increase fish oil to 15% and fishmeal to 40%. These fish require extruded floating pellets. In Africa, fishmeal is expensive, so use local byâproducts: poultry byâproduct meal (up to 20%) and blood meal (up to 10%). A practical trout growâout mix for a small farm: 30% fishmeal, 20% poultry byâproduct meal, 20% soybean meal, 15% wheat flour, 10% fish oil, 5% premix. Mix dry ingredients, add oil, then water to make a dough. Extrude through a 3â4 mm die. Dry at low temperature (below 60Â°C) to protect vitamins. Feed 2â3% body weight daily, split into 3â4 meals. Trout need clean, cold (12â18Â°C), oxygenârich water. In Kenya, farmers on Mount Kenya use this formula successfully. If you cannot get fish oil, use vegetable oil but reduce to 5% â too much vegetable oil causes fatty liver. For a 20 kg batch: 6 kg fishmeal, 4 kg poultry meal, 4 kg soybean meal, 3 kg wheat flour, 2 kg fish oil, 1 kg premix. This gives about 42% protein. Test by feeding a small group for two weeks and monitor growth. Salmon and trout are sensitive to aflatoxins in maize â always use fresh, mouldâfree maize. Store feed in a cool room; warm African temperatures spoil oil quickly.

lessons.title: Formulation for Carp and Other Cyprinids
lessons.body: Carp (common carp, grass carp, silver carp) are widely farmed in Africa, especially in Egypt and Nigeria. They are omnivorous and need 25â35% protein. A practical diet for common carp: 15% fishmeal, 25% soybean meal, 30% maize, 15% rice bran, 10% wheat offal, 5% premix. For grass carp, reduce fishmeal to 5% and increase plant materials like cassava leaves or water spinach to 20%. For silver carp, which filterâfeed, use fine powder (0.5 mm) with 20% fishmeal, 30% soybean meal, 30% rice bran, 20% maize. Carp feed can be sinking pellets or moist dough. In Egypt, farmers use a mix of 20% fishmeal, 30% soybean meal, 30% rice bran, 15% maize, 5% premix â this gives 28% protein. For a 100 kg batch: 20 kg fishmeal, 30 kg soybean meal, 30 kg rice bran, 15 kg maize, 5 kg premix. Grind all ingredients to a fine powder. Mix with water (about 25 litres) to form a stiff dough. Pass through a mincer with a 3 mm die. Dry in the sun for 2 days. Feed 3â4% body weight daily. Carp are bottom feeders, so sinking pellets are better. In polyculture, you can use the same feed for all cyprinids. Avoid overfeeding â uneaten feed fouls water. In Africa, many farmers use agricultural wastes like rice bran, which is cheap and available. But rice bran can go rancid; use within one month. For grass carp, add chopped fresh plants daily. Always keep water quality good: carp tolerate low oxygen but not pollution. Test your feed by dropping a pellet in water â it should sink slowly and remain intact for 20 minutes.

lessons.title: Formulation for Marine Shrimp
lessons.body: Marine shrimp (Penaeus species) are farmed in Africa, especially in Madagascar, Mozambique, and Nigeria. They need 35â45% protein and are carnivorous. A typical shrimp feed: 30% fishmeal, 20% squid meal, 15% soybean meal, 10% wheat flour, 10% fish oil, 5% shrimp meal, 5% vitaminâmineral premix, 5% lecithin. For a cheaper African version: 25% fishmeal, 15% shrimp meal, 20% soybean meal, 15% maize, 10% fish oil, 10% cassava flour, 5% premix. Shrimp feed must be extruded into sinking pellets of 1â2 mm for postlarvae, 3 mm for juveniles, 4 mm for adults. Use a feed mill with a fine die. In Madagascar, farmers use local fishmeal from bycatch. Mix dry ingredients, add oil, then water (about 30% of dry weight). Extrude and dry to <10% moisture. Feed 3â5% body weight daily, split into 4 meals. Shrimp are slow feeders; feed at dusk and dawn. For a 20 kg batch: 5 kg fishmeal, 4 kg shrimp meal, 4 kg soybean meal, 3 kg maize, 2 kg fish oil, 1 kg cassava flour, 1 kg premix. This gives about 40% protein. Shrimp need clean, salty water (15â30 ppt). In Africa, many farmers use artemia or local plankton to supplement. Never use poultry manure in shrimp ponds â it causes disease. Test feed by observing if shrimp eat it within 2 hours. Store feed in sealed bags; humidity ruins it. If you cannot get squid meal, replace with fishmeal but increase to 35%. Shrimp are sensitive to aflatoxins â use only fresh maize.

lessons.title: Formulation for Ornamental Fish
lessons.body: Ornamental fish (guppies, goldfish, cichlids, bettas) are a growing market in Africa. They need highâquality, smallâsized feed. For most ornamental fish, a 30â40% protein diet works. A simple recipe: 20% fishmeal, 20% shrimp meal, 20% soybean meal, 15% wheat flour, 10% spirulina, 10% fish oil, 5% vitaminâmineral premix. For bettas (carnivorous), increase fishmeal to 40% and shrimp meal to 20%. For goldfish (omnivorous), use 15% fishmeal, 15% shrimp meal, 30% soybean meal, 20% wheat flour, 10% spirulina, 5% fish oil, 5% premix. Grind all ingredients to a fine powder (0.2â0.5 mm). Mix with water to form a paste. Extrude through a fine mincer or use a garlic press to make tiny pellets. Dry in a dehydrator at 50Â°C or sunâdry on a mesh. For a 5 kg batch: 1 kg fishmeal, 1 kg shrimp meal, 1 kg soybean meal, 0.75 kg wheat flour, 0.5 kg spirulina, 0.5 kg fish oil, 0.25 kg premix. This gives about 35% protein. Feed 2â3% body weight daily, 2â3 times. Ornamental fish are sensitive to water quality; uneaten feed must be removed. In Africa, spirulina is available from Lake Chad. If not, use dried algae or spinach powder. For small fish, crush pellets between two spoons. Store in airtight jars away from light. Test by feeding a few fish â they should eat within 5 minutes. Never use stale feed; it causes fin rot. For breeding, add 5% freezeâdried bloodworms or brine shrimp. This formula works for most community tanks. Adjust for specific species: cichlids from Lake Malawi need more spirulina (15%).

quiz.q: What is the recommended crude protein level for tilapia fry (0.5â5 g)?
quiz.explanation: Tilapia fry require 35â40% protein for rapid growth.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is commonly used as a protein source in tilapia growâout feed in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Soybean meal is a widely available plant protein for tilapia.

quiz.q: How long should a good tilapia pellet hold together in water?
quiz.explanation: A quality pellet should remain intact for at least 30 minutes to reduce waste.

quiz.q: What is the maximum recommended inclusion of brewery waste in tilapia feed?
quiz.explanation: Brewery waste above 10% can degrade water quality.

quiz.q: For a 100 kg tilapia growâout batch, how much fishmeal is used in the example formula?
quiz.explanation: The growâout formula uses 15% fishmeal, so 15 kg for 100 kg.

quiz.q: What is the recommended protein level for catfish fry?
quiz.explanation: Catfish fry are carnivorous and need 45â50% protein.

quiz.q: Why should catfish feed be extruded (floating)?
options: B) Catfish feed at the surface
quiz.explanation: Catfish are surface feeders, so floating pellets are more accessible.

quiz.q: What is the maximum recommended level of blood meal in catfish feed?
quiz.explanation: Blood meal above 10% can cause vitamin deficiency.

quiz.q: In the catfish growâout formula, what is the percentage of groundnut cake?
quiz.explanation: The growâout mix includes 15% groundnut cake.

quiz.q: How often should catfish be fed?
quiz.explanation: Catfish are typically fed at dusk and dawn, twice daily.

quiz.q: What protein level do salmon and trout require?
quiz.explanation: Salmon and trout are carnivores needing 40â45% protein.

quiz.q: Which oil is preferred in salmon and trout feed?
quiz.explanation: Fish oil provides essential omegaâ3 fatty acids for coldâwater fish.

quiz.q: What is a suitable alternative to fishmeal in trout feed in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Poultry byâproduct meal is a local protein source that can replace part of fishmeal.

quiz.q: At what temperature should trout feed be dried to protect vitamins?
quiz.explanation: High temperatures destroy vitamins, so drying should be below 60Â°C.

quiz.q: What is the recommended feeding rate for trout?
quiz.explanation: Trout are typically fed 2â3% of body weight daily.

quiz.q: What protein level is suitable for common carp?
quiz.explanation: Carp are omnivorous and need 25â35% protein.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is increased for grass carp feed?
options: B) Plant materials like cassava leaves
quiz.explanation: Grass carp are herbivorous and thrive on plant materials.

quiz.q: What is the recommended pellet size for silver carp?
quiz.explanation: Silver carp are filter feeders and require fine powder (0.5 mm).

quiz.q: In the Egyptian carp formula, what is the percentage of rice bran?
quiz.explanation: The formula uses 30% rice bran.

quiz.q: Why should rice bran be used within one month?
quiz.explanation: Rice bran contains oils that can become rancid quickly.

quiz.q: What protein level do marine shrimp require?
quiz.explanation: Marine shrimp need 35â45% protein for optimal growth.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is a key protein source in shrimp feed?
quiz.explanation: Squid meal is highly digestible and rich in protein for shrimp.

quiz.q: What is the recommended feeding frequency for shrimp?
quiz.explanation: Shrimp are slow feeders and benefit from 4 small meals daily.

quiz.q: Why should poultry manure never be used in shrimp ponds?
quiz.explanation: Poultry manure can introduce pathogens and cause disease outbreaks.

quiz.q: What is the protein level for a typical shrimp feed formula given in the lesson?
quiz.explanation: The example formula yields about 40% protein.

quiz.q: What protein level is suitable for most ornamental fish?
quiz.explanation: Most ornamental fish do well on 30â40% protein.

quiz.q: Which ingredient is added for bettas?
quiz.explanation: Bettas are carnivorous, so fishmeal is increased to 40%.

quiz.q: What is the recommended particle size for ornamental fish feed?
quiz.explanation: Ornamental fish have small mouths and need fine powder or tiny pellets.

quiz.q: How should ornamental fish feed be stored?
options: B) In airtight jars away from light
quiz.explanation: Airtight, dark storage prevents spoilage and vitamin loss.

quiz.q: For cichlids from Lake Malawi, what should be increased in the feed?
quiz.explanation: Lake Malawi cichlids are herbivorous and need more spirulina (15%).
